podcast.title: Intervention in 5440 Stage Branding Dispute (c. 1997)
podcast.body: Raine Maida, the singer for Our Lady Peace, intervened to help 5440 resolve a dispute with promoters at a festival in Manitoba around 1997. 5440 refused to play due to a prominent Labatt's balloon on stage, violating their contract terms. Maida explained 5440's contractual clauses to the promoters, leading to the balloon's deflation and allowing 5440 to perform. "he hustles off with the promoters and other members of the band and explained to all these guys have this thing in their contract and you know, and he should take it down. So thanks to him, they took it down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fan Engagement
podcast.body: Duncan Coutts highlights the amazing energy the band receives from fans singing along "feverishly with every lyric." He notes that this phenomenon occurs even for the ninth song on an album, which probably never had a chance of being a single, demonstrating the deep connection and enthusiasm of their audience. "With our fans, you look out and really doesn't matter if it's the ninth song on the album that probably never has a chance of being a single and they're all singing along feverishly with every lyric."

podcast.title: First Demo Delivery
podcast.body: In the early 1990s, drummer Jeremy Taggart, then a shy teenager, personally presented the band's first-ever demo cassette to a radio station host. The demo was not given immediate attention but was later recognized for its historical significance. "It wasn't until much, much later that I realized that the kid with the big glasses was Jeremy Taggart, the drummer for RLAD Peace, and that he had presented me with the group's first ever demo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Inspired by Ray Kurzweil
podcast.body: Our Lady Peace are noted as big fans of inventor and thinker Ray Kurzweil, whose work at the intersection of music and artificial intelligence dates back to the mid-1960s. Kurzweil's technological concepts inspired the band in numerous ways, including the creation of their 2000 album, "Spiritual Machines." "Arlady Peace, big fans of inventor and thinker Ray Kurzweil, someone who was involved in something approaching the nexus of music and artificial intelligence as early as the mid-1960s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History and Future of AI in Music

podcast.title: Metadata Spelling Challenges – Acronyms
podcast.body: The band Our Lady Peace (OLP) is mentioned in the context of metadata spelling, highlighting the issue of whether to use the full name or its acronym, "R-L-A-D-P" or "O-L-P." "Do we write out R-L-A-D-P, or will O-L-P do?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Post-Can Rock Revolution Survival
podcast.body: Our Lady Peace were among the Canadian acts that continued to thrive long after the 1990s, showcasing the lasting impact of the Can Rock Revolution on Canadian music. "Many acts survived long after the decade ended. The tragically hip, Sloan, R80p, Serma Glockland, Tea Party, Matt Good, many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Summer Salt Festival Leader
podcast.body: Our Lady Peace spearheaded the Summer Salt festival, which took place in 1998 and again in 2000. This initiative was part of a burgeoning festival scene in Canada during the 1990s that showcased popular Canadian acts. "Summer Salt, spearheaded by Arlady Peace in 1998 and again in 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of the 90s CanRock Explosion

podcast.title: Summersault Festival Founder
podcast.body: Our Lady Peace initiated the Summersault festival in 1998, joining other artists in creating touring festivals during a financially flush period in the music industry. "Our Lady P started Summersault in 1998."

xref.title: Edwin Forms Crash Karma (2008)
xref.body: In 2008, Edwin partnered with Mike Turner (formerly of Our Lady Peace) and Jeff Burrows (of The Tea Party) to form the band Crash Karma. "Then in 2008, he joined up with Mike Turner, ex of our lady piece, and Jeff Burrows of the Tea Party in a band called Crash Karma."

xref.title: Archivist of Early Demos
xref.body: Years after Our Lady Peace's first demo was initially overlooked, guitarist Mike Turner was able to retrieve another copy of that original cassette from his archives, allowing it to be heard. "And after I told him the story, he was kind enough to go back into his archives and dig out another copy of that original demo."
